verdict: torch.compile is RULED OUT: the EAGER reference tracks the COMPILED reference within 0.0022 (50/50 within 0.03; both descend to ~0.090 at step49). RLinf (0.048) is below BOTH (only 31/50 within 0.03 of eager). The LR schedule is identical. The divergence is localized to GRADIENT MAGNITUDE: RLinf's grad_norm is systematically higher than the reference's (mean 2.42 vs 1.43; even at step0 on the same base weights, 2.39 vs 2.19), so with clip=1.0 and grad_norm<1.0 at later steps RLinf takes larger effective steps -> faster descent. Next: a same-batch gradient-norm parity comparison (like R15 did for the loss) to root-cause the grad_norm difference.
next_localization: same-batch gradient comparison: on an identical fixed batch + weights + noise/time, compare RLinf's vs the reference model's gradient norm (and per-layer grads) to determine whether the higher grad_norm is the data (RLinf rank-folded 256 unique vs reference 32) or the backward.
